solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cook’s last to assess meat, after a strike by one of the hands (6,4)

definitions.text: a strike by one of the hands

indicators.note: the last of the word Cook is its final letter
the rating of the meat comes after the A in the answer

blocks.note: the letter A, kept as printed
to rate something is to assess it
a chop is a cut of meat

annotation.surface: A cook sizing up the meat after the kitchen staff have gone on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: The strike looks like industrial action by the kitchen hands; it is a blow struck with the side of the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a sharp blow delivered with the edge of one hand.

entries.clue: Hoax one out to become criminal (9)

blocks.note: to kid someone is to hoax them
someone out cold having a nap

annotation.surface: A prankster whose hoax goes wrong and lands them on the wrong side of the law.
annotation.walkthrough: One out looks like someone excluded; here it is someone out for the count, asleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A kidnapper is a criminal who abducts people.

entries.clue: Book probing source subject of much SF (5)

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so the book sits inside the source

blocks.note: the root is the source of something
B is the abbreviation for book

annotation.surface: A book investigating where a staple of science fiction came from.
annotation.walkthrough: Book probing reads like a book that investigates; B simply probes into the middle of the source.
annotation.definitionFit: Robots are a staple subject of science fiction (SF), a definition by example.

entries.clue: Satisfied about limiting the French company putting damper on WFH (13)

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for satisfied is turned back
to limit something is to hem it in, so the reversed word encloses the next pieces

blocks.note: a need that is satisfied is met
Co is the abbreviation for company
to mute is to put a damper on

annotation.surface: A firm pleased with itself for discouraging working from home.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an office row about remote work, and the answer is exactly what the company is damping. WFH is the modern abbreviation for working from home.
annotation.definitionFit: WFH, working from home, is the everyday name for what telecommuting describes.

entries.clue: Top soldier concealing mistake upheld in court, right? (7)

indicators.note: the officer hides the mistake inside himself
in a down clue, held up means read bottom to top
that whole assembly goes inside the court

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
Ct is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A commanding officer covering up a blunder, with the verdict upheld in court.
annotation.walkthrough: Upheld looks like a court endorsing a ruling; in a down clue it turns the officer and his mistake upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Correct is a plain synonym of right, and the question mark lets the clue end on a query.

entries.clue: Vulgar science graduate, last to apologise, interrupts joke (7)

indicators.note: only the last letter of apologise is taken
to interrupt is to break into, so the pieces go into the middle of the joke

blocks.note: a joke is a good one, as in 'heard the one about...'

annotation.surface: A crude science graduate interrupting a joke and only apologising at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Joke has to be read as 'one', as in 'did you hear the one about...'.
annotation.definitionFit: Obscene is a plain synonym of vulgar in its sense of offensively crude.

entries.clue: Ruler suppressed in Communist’s ardour (4)

indicators.note: the ruler is held down inside the words that follow

blocks.note: straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: A monarch crushed by revolutionary fervour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is Russian history: communists did suppress the tsar, and here he is suppressed within their words.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruler is a general word; the tsar is one specific kind, the Russian emperor, so this is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Dramatic outlines: call for assistance about translation of Racine (9)

indicators.note: the call for help goes around the rest
translating turns the letters into a new form

annotation.surface: Someone crying for help over a translation of the French playwright Racine.
annotation.walkthrough: Racine the dramatist fits the theatrical surface, but his name is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film.

entries.clue: Friend, heading off after run, glowing with health? (5)

indicators.note: the friend's head, the first letter, goes off
the friend comes after the run

blocks.note: R is run in cricket scores

annotation.surface: A friend setting off after a run, flushed and fit.
annotation.walkthrough: Heading off looks like the friend leaving; it removes the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A ruddy complexion is a healthy red glow; the question mark admits it could be something else.

entries.clue: B&B in valley beside river — one not fully occupied? (7)

indicators.note: the Bs go inside the valley
the river goes next to it

annotation.surface: A bed and breakfast by a river in a valley, not fully booked.
annotation.walkthrough: The B&B with vacancies is not fully occupied; the definition means a person only half committed to something.
annotation.definitionFit: A dabbler takes up a pursuit only casually, never fully occupied with it.

entries.clue: Fear being overwhelmed by germ in algae (7)

indicators.note: the fear is swamped by, so inside, the germ

blocks.note: a germ is a seed, as in wheatgerm

annotation.surface: Fear of catching a germ lurking in pond algae.
annotation.walkthrough: Germ looks like a microbe; it is the germ of a plant, a seed.
annotation.definitionFit: Algae is the scientific group; seaweed is its most familiar example, the kind washed up on beaches.

entries.clue: Interstellar travel target adjusted at pre-launch — excellent to adopt that (5,8)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Mission control tweaking a star-bound craft's target before launch and approving it.
annotation.walkthrough: Excellent gives AI, which the adjusted letters must take in before the whole is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system, the usual goal proposed for interstellar travel.

entries.clue: Network uncovered in top-level location (5)

indicators.note: the outer letters, its cover, come off

blocks.note: LATTICE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A network exposed in a top-secret site.
annotation.walkthrough: Top-level sounds like high clearance; it is literally the top floor of a house.
annotation.definitionFit: Top-level is taken literally: the highest storey of a house, under the roof.

entries.clue: Perfect excuse briefly put forward around end of November (9)

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short of its last letter
the laying forward wraps the letter
only the last letter of November

blocks.note: to lay a proposal is to put it forward

annotation.surface: A flawless excuse, trimmed and offered late in November.
annotation.walkthrough: Excuse is the verb, as in excuse someone from duty, not an alibi.
annotation.definitionFit: Exemplary means fit to serve as a model, so perfect in the sense of beyond reproach.

entries.clue: Map user confused about following a topic in scientific discipline (4,11)

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of map user are mixed into a new order
the muddle goes around the rest

blocks.note: thematic means relating to a theme or topic

annotation.surface: A lost navigator mixed up about which subject a map belongs to.
annotation.walkthrough: Following a topic reads like tracking a subject; it defines an adjective, thematic.
annotation.definitionFit: Pure mathematics is maths studied for its own sake, one of the core disciplines of science.

entries.clue: Set up graduate function? It’s a complicated process (9)

blocks.note: to rig is to set up equipment

annotation.surface: Organising a graduation ceremony turns out to be a lot of bother.
annotation.walkthrough: Set up and function look like a graduation party; they are a verb and a job title.
annotation.definitionFit: Rigmarole is the informal word for a tiresomely long-winded procedure.

entries.clue: Wandering figure adopting new set unexpectedly (9)

indicators.note: the figure takes the others in

annotation.surface: A wanderer taking in a new set of companions out of the blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Set is the verb for a jelly firming up, not a group.
annotation.definitionFit: Strangely means in an unexpected way.

entries.clue: Academic mistaking surgeries for ops? (6,9)

indicators.note: the letters are taken wrongly, into a new order

annotation.surface: A don confusing a doctor's consulting sessions with operations.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder includes the little word for; a Regius professor holds a chair founded by the Crown at an old British university.
annotation.definitionFit: A Regius professor is a senior academic holding a royally endowed chair.

entries.clue: Fabulous bird, chicken, capturing duck in pictures (7)

indicators.note: the hen holds the duck inside
that goes inside the pictures

blocks.note: a duck is zero in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: Photographs of a wonderful bird: a chicken grabbing a duck.
annotation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means out of fable, not marvellous.
annotation.definitionFit: The phoenix is the mythical bird that rises from its own ashes.

entries.clue: Male interrupting individual mid-performance? (7)

indicators.note: the male breaks into the middle of the word

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer

annotation.surface: A man butting in on someone halfway through their act.
annotation.walkthrough: The male is a stag, not just any man.
annotation.definitionFit: The question mark flags a looser fit: while a show is under way, the actors are where the action is, in front of the audience.

entries.clue: International body’s hostility having secured nothing like complete agreement (9)

indicators.note: the hostility holds the nothing inside it

annotation.surface: The UN's quarrelling members achieving nothing like consensus.
annotation.walkthrough: Nothing like looks like 'not at all'; nothing is O and like belongs to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Like is doing the work of an adjective ending: unanimous describes a vote with total agreement.

entries.clue: Shade insensitive to neglect new artist (5)

indicators.note: the letter for new is left out

annotation.surface: A jaded critic ignoring a new artist's shading.
annotation.walkthrough: Insensitive is numb, and neglecting new drops its N.
annotation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, full shade.

entries.clue: Reduced pace of horse on course (5)

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

annotation.surface: A horse slowing to a trot on the racecourse.
annotation.walkthrough: Course looks like a racecourse; Royal Troon is a championship golf course on the west coast of Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: Troon is a famous links golf course in Ayrshire, Scotland.

entries.clue: I tucked into banned item, with spinning head (5)

indicators.note: tucked in like a napkin, so I goes inside the banned item
the whole thing turns round

annotation.surface: A contraband item, spun round with its head in a whirl.
annotation.walkthrough: Spinning head reads as dizzy; head is the definition and spinning is the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: Onion is slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion'.

entries.clue: Curse Rev’s way of projecting hurtful things? (7)

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it, and 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: A vicar's cursing as a way of hurling wounding words.
annotation.walkthrough: Rev looks like a vicar; it is revving an engine, gunning it. Hurtful things are darts, not insults.
annotation.definitionFit: A blowgun shoots darts by breath, a way of projecting things that hurt.

entries.clue: Insulting our group in a bad vibe (7)

indicators.note: our group sits in the vibe, inside its letters
a bad vibe is one gone wrong, so its letters go wrong too

annotation.surface: Rude remarks among friends creating a nasty atmosphere.
annotation.walkthrough: A bad vibe reads as a sour mood; bad is the signal to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Abusive language is insulting language, a plain synonym in the sense of verbal abuse.

entries.clue: Top part of church lacking second cross (4)

indicators.note: the named letter is left out

annotation.surface: The top of a church spire missing its second cross.
annotation.walkthrough: Top looks like it describes the part of the church; it is the definition. S for second is the time abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Top is used as a noun, the highest point of something, which is what the word from geometry means.

entries.clue: Former lover clearly gutted about writer, having long hidden desirability (10)

indicators.note: the inside letters are removed
the outer pieces go around the rest
long is tucked inside the writer

blocks.note: to be dying for something is to long for it

annotation.surface: An ex, obviously heartbroken over an author, secretly longing to be wanted.
annotation.walkthrough: Long is the verb, as in dying to do something, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Expediency is the quality of being advisable or desirable in the circumstances.
